instruction: What if I sold all my GameStop and Rivian and rolled the whole thing into VTI? Use cost basis (no live prices) and show me what my portfolio would look like before and after, with percentages. Use LibreOffice Calc to report this.
required_subtasks: List current BatBucks holdings with shares × avg_cost (read from holdings table)
Compute GME and RIVN position values at cost from the actual seeded shares × avg_cost
Sum the consolidation pool (GME value + RIVN value) using the agent's computed values
Divide the consolidation pool by VTI's avg_cost to determine new VTI shares to buy
Show the before/after portfolio composition by percentage
Note that current prices cannot be used (data issue) — calculation is on cost basis
Report the before/after portfolio comparison in LibreOffice Calc

rubrics.criterion: Agent computes the GameStop + Rivian cost-basis sum from the seeded holdings (GME shares × avg_cost + RIVN shares × avg_cost) and reports that consolidation pool figure
Agent reports the new total VTI position after the roll (existing VTI shares plus the additional shares funded by the GameStop+Rivian sell)
Presents a before/after portfolio composition with percentages showing how each position changes
Notes explicitly that the calculation uses cost basis (not market price) per the user's request
Agent lists Michael's current BatBucks holdings (live count from /api/holdings) with shares times avg_cost before computing the GameStop and Rivian sell pool
Agent divides the consolidation pool by VTI's avg_cost and reports the count of additional VTI shares to purchase from the GameStop+Rivian sell proceeds
Agent produces the before/after report in LibreOffice Calc (opens Calc, enters the portfolio data and percentages into a spreadsheet, and saves or presents the file)

instruction: Time to rebalance my BatBucks portfolio into something a financial advisor wouldn't laugh at. I'm aiming for roughly 60% VTI / 20% SBUX / 20% DIS across the blue-chip bucket at cost basis (RIVN stays put — I'm not touching that one). Sell every share of GME I'm holding to free up cash, then use that plus my free cash to buy enough VTI to push the allocation toward 60%. Do this as a cost-basis rebalance, not live prices. Exact percentages aren't required — a reasonable approximation toward the 60/20/20 shape is the goal.
required_subtasks: Open BatBucks and review all current holdings (live count from /api/holdings) at cost basis
Record the total portfolio value at cost (sum holdings × avg_cost) and current cash balance
Place a sell order for the full GME share count shown in holdings
Confirm the sell order and verify cash balance increased (the sell executes at market price, not cost basis)
Compute a VTI buy quantity that pushes VTI toward ~60% of the rebalanced blue-chip (VTI+SBUX+DIS) cost-basis total (RIVN held out of the target bucket)
Place a buy order for the computed VTI share quantity
Open the holdings view and confirm the new allocation (GME=0, VTI increased)

rubrics.criterion: Agent reads all current BatBucks holdings (live count from /api/holdings) and records each ticker's avg_cost value at cost basis before placing any orders
Agent sells every GME share Michael holds (full position liquidation) in a single or combined order

Agent computes a VTI buy quantity that pushes VTI toward approximately 60% of the rebalanced blue-chip (VTI+SBUX+DIS) cost-basis total, treating the 60/20/20 target as an approximation (RIVN held out of the target bucket)
Agent places a VTI buy order for the computed quantity
Agent confirms new holdings row shows GME=0 and VTI shares increased
Agent explicitly uses cost-basis framing (not market value)
Agent verifies the GME sell order and VTI buy order persist in the BatBucks order history and that the holdings table reflects the rebalance with cash updated

instruction: I want downside protection on every position I'm holding in BatBucks. Put a couple Stop order on each one at 15% below what I paid for it, just to give me a floor. Then build me a new watchlist called 'Oscar's Picks' with eight big-name ETFs in it. Make sure the stop-losses actually show up in my open orders and the watchlist is still there if I refresh.
required_subtasks: Open BatBucks and note all current holdings (live count from /api/holdings) and their avg_cost values
Place a Stop order (single stop price; not Stop-Limit) for each held ticker at ~15% below its actual avg_cost (from holdings)
Create a new watchlist named 'Oscar's Picks'
Add 8 big-name ETF tickers to the watchlist (e.g., VTI, VOO, QQQ, SPY, DIA, IWM, VEA, VWO or comparable large-AUM ETFs)
Reload the page and confirm stop-losses and watchlist both persist

rubrics.criterion: Agent opens BatBucks and lists all current holdings (live count from /api/holdings) with their avg_cost values to plan the stop-loss orders
Agent submits a Stop order (single stop price, not Stop-Limit) for every current BatBucks holding (live count from /api/holdings) at ~15% under each ticker's actual avg_cost (computed from holdings)
Agent creates a new BatBucks watchlist named 'Oscar's Picks'
Agent adds 8 big-name/mainstream ETF tickers (e.g., VTI, VOO, QQQ, SPY, DIA, IWM, VEA, VWO or comparable large-AUM broad-market ETFs) to the 'Oscar's Picks' watchlist in BatBucks

Agent reloads BatBucks and confirms stop-loss orders are accounted for (open or filled) for each current holding — noting that any stop placed below the current trading price may fill immediately — and the 'Oscar's Picks' watchlist persists after refresh

instruction: Take a look at my brokerage portfolio. How bad is my meme-stock problem, and what would a sensible rebalance look like that doesn't totally abandon the names I actually like? Use cost basis, not market prices. While you're at it, peek at my old WUPHF investment agreement in ~/Downloads/ — that one was the OG mistake, and it sets the pattern for how I get into these things. Return the review of my portfolio in LibreOffice Writer.
required_subtasks: Open BatBucks and pull Michael's current RIVN position (shares and avg_cost) from the holdings view / /api/holdings
Report Michael's total RIVN cost-basis exposure (shares × avg_cost from /api/holdings)
List all current holdings (live count from /api/holdings) with shares and avg_cost
Compute each position's cost-basis value (shares × avg_cost) and report RIVN's share of the total cost-basis portfolio
Recommend a RIVN-trim plan that respects Michael's existing preference for narrative/consumer names like DIS and SBUX (don't suggest dumping into pure index)
Open ~/Downloads/WUPHF_Investment_Agreement.txt to ground the 'OG mistake pattern' framing in the trim proposal

rubrics.criterion: Agent pulls Michael's BatBucks RIVN holding (shares and avg_cost from the holdings view / /api/holdings) and reports it as the source of his RIVN exposure
Agent reports Michael's RIVN cost-basis dollar exposure (shares × avg_cost from live BatBucks holdings) and expresses RIVN's share as a percent of the total cost-basis portfolio
Agent frames the analysis using cost basis (avg_cost) per the user's request, not market value
Agent proposes a RIVN trim plan consistent with Michael's historical consumer-brand bias (preserves DIS/SBUX-style narrative names rather than suggesting a pure-index dump)
Agent reports the BatBucks holdings rows as the data source for the trim recommendation instead of inventing numbers
Agent delivers the full RIVN trim answer including cost-basis concentration percent and recommendation without abandoning the task midway
Agent opens ~/Downloads/WUPHF_Investment_Agreement.txt and references it as the founding 'bad bet' pattern that explains the current RIVN over-exposure
Agent produces the portfolio review in a LibreOffice Writer document, as requested in the instruction

instruction: What's my total BatBucks portfolio worth at cost basis across everything I'm holding, and how much cash is sitting in the account?
required_subtasks: Open BatBucks and list all current holdings (live count from /api/holdings)
Compute portfolio value at cost basis (shares * avg_cost per position)
Read off the cash balance
Report the total and cash

rubrics.criterion: Agent reports Michael's BatBucks portfolio value at cost basis (sum of shares × avg_cost across all current holdings, live count from /api/holdings)
Agent reports the cash balance in the BatBucks account separately from holdings value
Agent uses cost basis (avg_cost) framing as the user requested, not market value
Agent reconciles the reported BatBucks cost-basis total and cash balance against the holdings table rows instead of fabricating numbers

instruction: Trim my GameStop position in half and roll the proceeds into VTI. I'm trying to be less of a degenerate about this.
required_subtasks: Open BatBucks and read the live GME share count from the holdings table
Sell roughly half of the live GME shares (round up or down by one)
Use the proceeds to buy additional VTI shares
Verify the positions update correctly

rubrics.criterion: Agent sells approximately half of the live GME position (roughly half the seeded share count, rounding up or down by one share) as the half-position trim into VTI
Agent buys VTI using proceeds from the GME sale (not cash from elsewhere)
Agent confirms both GameStop sell and VTI buy orders executed and verifies the updated BatBucks positions reflect the half-GME trim rebalance
Agent opens BatBucks and reports the existing GameStop GME position share count (read from the live holdings table) before executing the half-trim sell into VTI
